dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef001 μ X K A says that X is measurable, K is positive, the real-valued function ω ↦ exp((X ω)^2 / K^2) is integrable with respect to μ, and its integral is at most A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expands the second equivalence into equivalence of existence of positive scale parameters giving an exponential-square moment bound with right-hand constant 2 and with right-hand constant A; the outer positivity condition on K duplicates positivity inside this definition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef002 μ X K A says that X is measurable, K is positive, and for every real t ≥ 0, the real value of μ({ω | |X ω| ≥ t}) is at most A · exp(-(t^2)/(K^2)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expands the first equivalence into equivalence of existence of positive scale parameters giving a Gaussian tail bound with prefactor 2 and with prefactor A; the outer positivity condition on K duplicates positivity inside this definition.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: And P Q is the conjunction requiring both propositions P and Q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires both the tail-bound equivalence and the exponential-moment equivalence, and it also combines the component conditions inside each existential property.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Exists p asserts that there is a witness for which the predicate p holds.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each side of each equivalence has its own existentially chosen real scale K; no witness is shared or quantitatively related across sides or between the two equivalences.

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: Iff P Q means that P implies Q and Q implies P.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It asserts separate bidirectional equivalences between existence with constant 2 and existence with constant A for the tail property and for the moment property.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: LT.lt is the less-than relation supplied by the relevant ordered type instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real numbers it expresses A > 1 and K > 0, which restrict the admissible bound constant and scale witnesses.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measurable-space structure on Ω specifies which subsets of Ω are measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the measurable structure used by μ, by measurability of X, and by the events occurring in the tail bound.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: IsProbabilityMeasure μ asserts that μ is a probability measure, in particular that the total mass is one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the universal measure μ to probability measures and ensures event masses are finite probabilities.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instNeZeroSucc

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the mass of the tail event a real quantity comparable with A · exp(-t^2/K^2); probability finiteness avoids loss from converting an infinite value.

binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
An arbitrary measure μ on Ω, together with the assumption that μ is a probability measure.
An arbitrary function X : Ω → ℝ.
conclusions: There exists a real K > 0 such that X is measurable and, for every real t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |X(ω)| ≥ t}), viewed as a real number, is at most 2 exp(-t²/K²), if and only if there exists a (not necessarily equal) real K > 0 such that X is measurable and the corresponding bound holds with A in place of 2.

There exists a real K > 0 such that X is measurable, ω ↦ exp(X(ω)²/K²) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2, if and only if there exists a (not necessarily equal) real K > 0 such that X is measurable, that exponential-square function is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most A.
mathematical_definitions: For K > 0 and C ∈ ℝ, the tail property is: X is measurable and ∀ t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |X(ω)| ≥ t}) ≤ C exp(-t²/K²), where the measure value is converted from an extended nonnegative real to a real number.
For K > 0 and C ∈ ℝ, the exponential-moment property is: X is measurable, exp(X²/K²) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(X(ω)²/K²) dμ(ω) ≤ C.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On every probability space, for every real-valued function X and every A > 1, admitting some positive scale for a Gaussian tail estimate with multiplicative constant 2 is equivalent to admitting some positive scale for the same kind of estimate with multiplicative constant A; independently, admitting some positive scale for an integrable exponential-square moment bounded by 2 is equivalent to admitting some positive scale for such a moment bounded by A. The positive scale may be chosen separately in every existential assertion.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem is restricted to probability measures and to constants A > 1.
Every scale K must be strictly positive; this positivity is asserted both outside and inside each local definition, so it is redundant but unambiguous.
The tail inequality is required only for thresholds t ≥ 0.

The witnesses K on the two sides of an equivalence are independent, and the witnesses used for the tail and moment equivalences are also independent; no common K or quantitative conversion between scales is asserted.
The statement asserts no implication or equivalence between the tail property and the exponential-moment property; it only conjoins two separate invariance-under-changing-the-constant assertions.
Each biconditional may hold because both existential propositions are false. In particular, if X is not measurable, every local property is false and both biconditionals are vacuously true.
For measurable X that satisfies neither version of a given tail or moment property, that particular biconditional is likewise true by false/false equivalence.
The exponential-moment condition separately requires integrability, so the integral inequality is not being used alone with any default value for a nonintegrable function.
The use of Measure.real converts event masses to real values; under the probability-measure assumption these masses are finite.
No centering, mean-zero condition, independence assumption, symmetry assumption, or finiteness condition beyond those explicitly contained in the two local properties is encoded.
